transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Clarke (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM); Lena Morales (Mariner - Head of ML), Tom Briggs (Mariner - Platform), Ibrahim Khan (Mariner - Procurement), Asha Patel (Mariner - Security)

Summary: Quick renewal + expansion check-in. Customer is mid-contract, seeking 20% capacity uplift, EU-edge nodes for EU shopfronts, and a one-year contract extension with predictable pricing. Discussed dedicated pool sizing, burst capacity, SLOs for EU region, KMS integration, and next steps to finalize commercials and run a short benchmark.

Topics: renewal/pricing, capacity bump (20%), EU-edge onboarding, private data residency concerns, security docs, benchmark timeline, contract redlines.

Transcript body:
[15:00] Sophie Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — we wanted to align on the renewal and the EU-edge ask. How's the week, Lena?
[15:12] Lena Morales: Good, thanks. Sorry, running a little behind this morning. Appreciate you pulling this together. We got budget approval on the core renewal but we need clarity on the EU-edge pricing and the burst behavior for Black Friday-like peaks.
[15:27] Sophie Clarke: Understood. Ravi, do you want to run through the proposed dedicated pool config and how burst works?
[15:33] Ravi Patel: Yeah, sure. So from a runtime side, we recommend a baseline dedicated pool sized to handle steady-state spiky TPS, in Mariner's case looks like 120 concurrent generation streams during peak, so we suggested a 20% headroom bump on top of current reserved. Bursts are handled by short-lived shared capacity — that's the default fallback — but for EU-edge we can configure a local warm pool for much faster cold-starts.
[15:56] Tom Briggs: Wait, by "shared capacity" do you mean the hosted multi-tenant tiers? We have data residency constraints, so we need the EU-edge requests to stay in eu-west unless overflow is explicit and encrypted.
[16:09] Ravi Patel: Right, good call. For EU-edge we can route by region and policy. Overflow can be set to fall back to EU-dedicated, or if the dedicated is saturated we can route to a fallthrough hosted instance that also pins to eu-west. There is an additional cost for pinned eu-west hosted capacity; Sophie will detail that in pricing.
[16:28] Ibrahim Khan: From procurement perspective we also want the renewal to lock pricing for 12 months and have a clear SLA for latency 95th percentile. Can you commit to that?
[16:38] Sophie Clarke: Yeah, we can do a 12-month fixed pricing for the reserved capacity component. For SLAs we have standard latency SLOs for Dedicated — we can add a 95th percentile target in the contract for the dedicated pool. The hosted fallback has different SLOs; we'll flag that in the document.
[16:58] Asha Patel: Also, encryption questions. We use a customer-managed KMS in AWS for keys. Does Redwood support external KMS/HSM? And how do audit logs look for private EU-edge traffic?
[17:10] Ravi Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS via IAM roles, and for on-prem or VPC options we can support HSM/KMS through our Private offering. Audit logs for inference calls are available — token-level logs are redacted by default but we can enable full request/response logging for customers with appropriate controls. There is an extra retention fee for longer audit retention.
[17:34] Lena Morales: Hmm ok. What's the timeline to have the EU-edge nodes live if we greenlight now?
[17:41] Sophie Clarke: For a standard EU-edge onboarding with reserved capacity and basic networking (VPC peering), we usually see 3-4 weeks. If you want HSM integration and longer audit retention, add 1-2 weeks to accommodate security reviews and cert provisioning.
[17:56] Tom Briggs: We also want to validate throughput for our 6k tokens average requests — do you have a quick bench we can run?
[18:05] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll run a 5k-6k token throughput run with quantized model paths to mimic your workload. I'll use staging region eu-west-1 and share results and traces. Expect to see per-token p50/p95 numbers and cost-impact for quant vs fp16.
[18:20] Lena Morales: That would be great. Also a note — we've been testing the new reranking flow and saw some variability after last month's rollout. Curious about how Redwood handles model rollouts across regions.
[18:33] Jordan Kim: On rollouts: we provide canary and A/B rollout controls in the console; you can pin traffic percentages by model version and region. If you prefer, we can do an automatic fallback to last-known-good model under regressions. We also surface regression alerts tied to evals.
[18:52] Tom Briggs: Nice. On the pricing side, Sophie, can you share a line item for the dedicated pool, EU-edge premium, and hosted fallback? We need it split by monthly committed and overage/burst rates.
[19:04] Sophie Clarke: Absolutely. I'll send a detailed quote. For transparency, we'll show per-token unit economics, reserved flat fee, dedicated instance hourly, and overage/burst multipliers. i'm going to include an optional 15% discount for a 12-month commitment if you sign by end of the month.
[19:21] Ibrahim Khan: Procurement will need NET30 terms and a PO. Also, can you include a clause about data residency and KMS in the SOW?
[19:29] Sophie Clarke: We'll include explicit SOW language and KMS appendix. Legal usually wants the redline session — propose next Thurs?
[19:36] Ibrahim Khan: That works. 2027-02-25?
[19:38] Sophie Clarke: I'll set it up.
[19:40] Asha Patel: One more security thing — do you have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO certs? We need to store them in our vendor portal.
[19:48] Jordan Kim: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. I'll upload the latest artifacts to your portal and share direct links as well.
[19:58] Lena Morales: ok great. circling back to the capacity numbers: we said 20% bump — is that on top of current reserved, or total?
[20:08] Ravi Patel: It's additive on top of current reserved. But Sophie and I will model two variants: a conservative 12% uplift and a more comfortable 20% uplift with a small burst buffer. We'll show cost delta for both.
[20:21] Tom Briggs: For the benchmark, can you include KV cache warmup patterns? Our live traffic has a high repetition rate for product descriptions.
[20:31] Ravi Patel: Yep, I'll simulate prefix caching and include tests with and without prefix/KV cache to showcase cost savings and latency improvements.
[20:41] Lena Morales: Perfect. That helps our budget case. Also heads up, MegaCloud AI procurement flagged a discounted comparison — don't want to be surprised if they bring a competing price.
[20:51] Sophie Clarke: Noted — we'll make the value vs price explicit: per-token latency, regional guarantees, and observability differences.
[20:58] Ibrahim Khan: Anything else?
[21:02] Sophie Clarke: Quick recap: Action items — I'll send quote with EU-edge line item and optional discount, Ravi will run the benchmark and share results, Jordan will upload security docs and prepare onboarding checklist. We'll schedule legal redline for 2027-02-25. If that works we'll aim to sign and start provisioning by early March.
[21:18] Lena Morales: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[21:21] Sophie Clarke: Thanks all — we'll follow up by email with the materials.

End of call.
